q1: SELECT DISTINCT AUTHOR_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS WHERE AUTHOR_ID = VIEWER_ID ORDER BY ID
q2: SELECT AUTHOR_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS WHERE AUTHOR_ID = VIEWER_ID GROUP BY ID ORDER BY ID ASC , COUNT(ID) DESC

q2_prompt_sql: SELECT AUTHOR_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS WHERE AUTHOR_ID = VIEWER_ID GROUP BY ID ORDER BY ID ASC , COUNT(ID) DESC
counterexample: INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (1, 101, 201, '2023-01-01'); INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (2, 101, 301, '2023-01-02'); INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (3, 102, 201, '2023-01-03');
explanation: Q1 selects distinct AUTHOR_IDs where AUTHOR_ID = VIEWER_ID, and orders the results by ID. Q2 does the same but also groups the results by ID and orders by ID ASC and COUNT(ID) DESC. The difference arises when there are multiple rows with the same AUTHOR_ID, as Q2 will order by the count of ID in descending order, which can change the final order of results compared to Q1.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have multiple rows with the same AUTHOR_ID, and the VIEWER_ID should be different for at least one of these rows. The difference in results will be visible when the count of ID is not the same for all AUTHOR_IDs.
